fatal_errors: The proposed nanoflake coating is unrelated to the target intervention of varying Mo content in a Ni/MoS2-Ag-Cr2O3-containing CoCrFeNiMox composite.
The cited evidence concerns spray-coated steel tested in ambient conditions and does not establish coating survival or lubrication on CoCrFeNi at temperatures approaching 800 °C.
Formation of an amorphous-carbon-rich film is asserted under dry ambient sliding without identifying a carbon precursor; the cited evidence instead shows strong solvent dependence.

The hypothesis predicts simultaneous friction and wear improvement at every temperature, whereas the target system exhibits different composition optima for friction and wear and severe intermediate-temperature wear.
explanation: The response addresses the broad objective and proposes one intervention with a controlled comparison and a usable falsification rule. It is not a reconstruction of the hidden study: it omits the Mo0.2–Mo1 compositional series, SPS processing, lubricant and oxide additives, sigma-phase strengthening, and temperature-dependent MoS2/Ag and oxide–silver-molybdate tribofilms. Test conditions and boundaries are largely unquantified. Most importantly, E1 supports room-temperature ambient performance on a steel tribopair, not wide-temperature performance on CoCrFeNi, while E2 demonstrates that performance depends strongly on coating solvent and therefore undercuts the claim of general environmental adaptability. The extrapolation to 800 °C and the proposed carbon/oxide-film chemistry are consequently unsupported, despite the experiment being reasonably discriminating.
